description: productEvents (explicit mode): each case starts an interaction (startInteraction(interaction) under config), then runs steps in order: "span" ends that span through the span processor created with productEvents (its onEnd only; the span already carries rudderstack.interaction_id as onStart would set it), "wrapper_call" calls interaction.recordCall with the call fields plus its window and then recordToolCall(toolCallIds) when it was recorded, "end" ends the interaction (responseText optional), "flush" awaits the span processor's forceFlush. config: captureContent, emitLlmCalls, toolBreakdown and prices go to configure(); the span processor is always created with the in-memory client (ai_otel_span events it exports are not compared); analytics "processor_only" also clears the configure() client (configure({ analytics: null })), otherwise the same client is the configure() client; classifier { intents?, outcomes?, classify: { intent?, outcome?, intent_summary? }, delay_ms? } is configure({ classifier: { classify, intents, outcomes } }) with a classify that returns those fields after delay_ms. Span, event and wrapper-call times are nanoseconds based at 1760000000000000000; drivers add (wall clock in ns taken just before the interaction starts) - 1760000000000000000 to every one of them. expected is every product event in order, without timestamp/messageId, context.wrapperLibrary without name/version, latency_ms, time_to_first_token_ms and classifier_duration_ms replaced by "<number>". config.perCallContent (SDK-6798, default false): keep call_index in ai_llm_response_received; without it drivers delete call_index from those events before comparing, so older cases need not list it. With captureContent and emitLlmCalls the span input and output become input_messages, output_text and output_tool_calls. SDK-6898 lifecycle additions: "span_start" runs onStart for ancestry before any end; "span_on_end" schedules onEnd in an interaction finalizer; "shutdown" awaits processor shutdown; "sdk_flush" awaits the SDK flush. config.advanceClock (default false) advances the portable wall clock to the maximum span start/end seen so far; "end" uses that clock as interaction end. "advance_clock" sets the clock from timeUnixNano; "expect_recorded_calls" asserts the number of model calls already recorded at that checkpoint. config.exactCallTiming keeps numeric per-call latency/TTFT and adds timestampOffsetMs relative to the interaction clock base to expected call events. Existing cases keep their original clocks. Prep tolerance is 1 ms, inclusive; overlapping windows are inclusive. Generated by ai-sdk-node test/tracing/product-events-conformance.test.ts.

cases.name: sdk6898_review_open_tool_preserves_A_B_order
cases.description: A finishes with an open tool descendant, then independent B finishes. Calls are recorded immediately as A=1, B=2 before the tool ends.

cases.name: sdk6898_usage_parent_zero_usage_child_without_response_id
cases.description: A usage parent stays counted when its overlapping same-model descendant has no usage attributes or response ID; the richer parent and zero-usage child both count.

cases.name: sdk6898_wrapper_twin_nested_child_keeps_wrapper_tokens_and_event
cases.description: A wrapper call merges with its span twin behind a pending prep span. The nested child cannot suppress the wrapper: both calls count, wrapper usage remains authoritative at 100 tokens, and its delayed call event survives. The pure prep span is suppressed using the surviving wrapper twin as evidence.
